Container.Name: strawberry-notes-aio
Container.Overview:
Self-hosted, MIT-licensed, multi-user, AI-native rich-text notes app — all-in-one image. One container: no separate Postgres container to run yourself, no AUTH_SECRET to generate up front. Point it at any Postgres 17+ server you already have (a shared instance is fine) and it migrates its own schema on first boot.
This image does NOT bundle Postgres. You need a reachable Postgres 17+ server first:
1. On that Postgres server, create a role and database Strawberry will own (run as a superuser, once):
CREATE ROLE strawberry LOGIN PASSWORD '<long-random-string>'; CREATE DATABASE strawberry OWNER strawberry;
2. Fill in DATABASE_URL below with that role/database, e.g. postgres://strawberry:<password>@192.168.1.20:5432/strawberry
3. Leave AUTH_SECRET blank — the container generates one into /data/.auth_secret on first boot and reuses it on every restart. (Set it yourself instead if you'd rather manage it externally.)
4. First-time admin: set ALLOW_PUBLIC_SIGNUP to `true`, deploy, visit /signup and create your account (first user becomes admin), then flip it back to `false` and redeploy. Or use the operator CLI: `docker exec -it strawberry-notes-aio npm run user:create -- you@example.com`.
Semantic search needs the `pgvector` extension on your Postgres server — it is OPTIONAL. Without it, everything else works normally and semantic search / the embedding worker just stay disabled (checked once at boot; see the container log for "pgvector not available"). Postgres 13+ and pgvector 0.5+ let the database OWNER role (not just a superuser) run `CREATE EXTENSION vector` itself, so if your shared server already has pgvector installed, migrations pick it up automatically — no extra step needed beyond the CREATE ROLE / CREATE DATABASE above.
Runs as UID 1001 / GID 1001 — see the /data path description below.
Docs: https://github.com/straplocked/strawberry-notes/tree/main/docs/technical/deployment.md
Container.Requires: A reachable Postgres 17+ server (17 recommended; 13+ works). Does NOT need to be on this Unraid box — DATABASE_URL just needs to resolve from inside this container. pgvector is optional; see the Overview.

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: Host port the WebUI is published on. Default: 3200.

Config.Name: DATABASE_URL
Config.Description: Full Postgres connection string for a role that OWNS its database (CREATE ROLE strawberry LOGIN PASSWORD '...'; CREATE DATABASE strawberry OWNER strawberry;). Strawberry runs migrations against it on every boot. Plain Postgres 17 works; pgvector is optional (see Overview).

Config.Name: AUTH_SECRET
Config.Description: Leave blank to auto-generate on first boot (saved to /data/.auth_secret and reused across restarts). Set it explicitly only if you want to manage the secret yourself or share it across replicas.

Config.Name: AUTH_URL
Config.Description: Public URL where Strawberry is reachable, e.g. https://notes.example.com. Leave blank for LAN access; set explicitly when behind a TLS-terminating proxy that strips X-Forwarded-* headers.

Config.Name: ALLOW_PUBLIC_SIGNUP
Config.Description: Set to `true` for the initial install so you can create your admin account at /signup, then flip back to `false` and redeploy. Leave `false` afterwards unless you want strangers to register.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Uploaded images AND the auto-generated AUTH_SECRET live here. Survives container recreates — do not delete. Must be writable by UID 1001 / GID 1001 (chown -R 1001:1001 on that path before first boot if Unraid created it as nobody:users).

Config.Name: MAX_UPLOAD_MB
Config.Description: Per-file upload size cap in megabytes.

Config.Name: REQUIRE_EMAIL_CONFIRMATION
Config.Description: When true, signup creates accounts unconfirmed and emails a confirmation link. Implies SMTP must be configured below.

Config.Name: SMTP_HOST
Config.Description: SMTP relay hostname for password-reset and notification emails. Leave blank to disable email entirely.

Config.Name: SMTP_PORT
Config.Description: SMTP port. 587 (STARTTLS) is most common; 465 with SMTP_SECURE=true for implicit TLS.

Config.Name: SMTP_USER
Config.Description: Optional SMTP auth username.

Config.Name: SMTP_PASS
Config.Description: Optional SMTP auth password.

Config.Name: SMTP_FROM
Config.Description: From: address on outbound mail. Required when SMTP_HOST is set.

Config.Name: SMTP_SECURE
Config.Description: `true` forces implicit TLS at connect time (port 465 deployments).

Config.Name: EMBEDDING_ENDPOINT
Config.Description: OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint (`/v1`). Leave blank to disable semantic search; everything else still works. Also requires pgvector on your Postgres server — see Overview.

Config.Name: EMBEDDING_MODEL
Config.Description: Model id, e.g. text-embedding-3-small (OpenAI) or nomic-embed-text (Ollama).

Config.Name: EMBEDDING_API_KEY
Config.Description: Bearer token for the embeddings provider. Optional for local providers like Ollama.

Config.Name: EMBEDDING_DIMS
Config.Description: Vector dimension. MUST match the provider's output dim. Default 1024 matches mxbai-embed-large and similar.

Config.Name: PASSWORD_AUTH
Config.Description: Email/password sign-in. Set to `false` for OIDC-only or proxy-only deployments.

Config.Name: TOTP_ENABLED
Config.Description: Enable per-user TOTP/2FA enrollment from Settings → Security.

Config.Name: OIDC_ENABLED
Config.Description: Enable OIDC SSO. Requires the four OIDC_* fields below.

Config.Name: OIDC_ISSUER
Config.Description: OIDC issuer URL, e.g. https://auth.example.com/application/o/strawberry/

Config.Name: OIDC_CLIENT_ID
Config.Description: OIDC client id.

Config.Name: OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET
Config.Description: OIDC client secret.

Config.Name: OIDC_NAME
Config.Description: Label for the SSO sign-in button on /login.

Config.Name: OIDC_AUTO_PROVISION
Config.Description: JIT-create local users on first OIDC sign-in (requires the IdP to set email_verified=true).

Config.Name: OIDC_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING
Config.Description: DANGER: auto-link OIDC sign-ins to existing email-matching local users. Account-takeover risk if your IdP allows arbitrary email assignment. Off by default.

Config.Name: PROXY_AUTH
Config.Description: Bypass first-party login and trust a forward-auth header (Authentik forward-auth, Authelia, oauth2-proxy). Hides /login. Requires PROXY_AUTH_SHARED_SECRET.

Config.Name: PROXY_AUTH_USER_HEADER
Config.Description: Header carrying the trusted username.

Config.Name: PROXY_AUTH_EMAIL_HEADER
Config.Description: Optional companion email header.

Config.Name: PROXY_AUTH_SHARED_SECRET
Config.Description: REQUIRED when PROXY_AUTH=true. The proxy must forward `X-Forward-Auth-Secret: <this>` on every request; mismatch → 401. Distinguishes proxy traffic from clients spoofing the username header.

Config.Name: PROXY_AUTH_LOGOUT_URL
Config.Description: Where the sign-out button points in proxy mode (e.g. /outpost.goauthentik.io/sign_out for Authentik forward-auth). Unset → button hidden.
